description: Behavior evals — given a request, does the skill produce a valid, well-formed Claude Code agent file?

evals.name: readonly-security-agent
evals.prompt: Create an agent that scans a repo for hardcoded secrets and credentials and reports findings. It should never modify files, just read and report.
evals.expected_output: A file agents/<name>.agent.md with valid frontmatter (name, description, model, color, tools) where tools are read-only (no Write/Edit), a 'When to invoke' section with 2-4 prose scenarios, an output contract, and a Rules section that includes a never-modify boundary.

assertions.text: Output is a single Markdown file named agents/<name>.agent.md
Frontmatter contains all five keys: name, description, model, color, tools
name is lowercase, hyphen-separated, 3-50 chars, starts and ends alphanumeric
tools array is read-only — contains no Write or Edit
description states triggering conditions and names 2-4 scenarios
Body has a 'When to invoke' section with 2-4 prose bullet scenarios
Body defines an output contract (what the agent returns)
Rules section includes a never-modify-files boundary
System prompt is written in second person ("You are...")

evals.name: code-generation-agent
evals.prompt: I want a subagent that takes a function and writes unit tests for it, then runs them until they pass. Put it in the workflows plugin.
evals.expected_output: An agent file saved under plugins/workflows/agents/ with tools that allow writing code and running tests (Write/Edit + Bash), an input contract describing what the agent receives, a process with iterate-until-green logic, and an output contract.

assertions.text: tools include Bash (to run tests) and Write or Edit (to author tests)
Body defines an input contract (what the agent is given)
Process describes running tests and iterating until they pass
description names 2-4 trigger scenarios and points to 'When to invoke'

evals.name: skill-not-agent-redirect
evals.prompt: Create an agent I can run with /changelog that I trigger manually to generate a changelog from recent commits.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this is a user-triggered slash command (a skill), not an autonomous agent, and surfaces the distinction — either redirecting to creating a skill or explicitly confirming the user still wants an agent before scaffolding one.

assertions.text: Response flags that a manually-triggered /command is a skill, not an agent
Does not silently scaffold an agent without surfacing the skill-vs-agent distinction
